In Xbox360 gamepad language here are the mappings

LeftStick = Actor move

RightStick = Camera rotation
RightStickButton = Jump
Dpad = move camera X Y
R/L Trigger = Camera zoom
Right bumper = Next camera #
Left Bumper = Previous camera #
Y = random whole body animation
X = random upper body animation
A = random lower body animation
B = actor look at camera

This is all experimental so let me know how you would like it to work etc-

notes.title: You can now use your own models in Nightmare Puppeteer
notes.content:
Here's a video showing the basics of importing 3d models into Nightmare Puppeteer

[previewyoutube=FrTKkc1eAno;full][/previewyoutube]

With the latest build on the "testy" branch you can test this out today!

[url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/NightmarePuppeteerPublic/blob/master/Add3dModelsReadMe.md]Here's what you need to know[/url] about importing into Nightmare Puppeteer

[b]TLDR[/b]
[list]
*Fbx's for characters from these programs/sites supported- Daz 3d, iClone Character Creator, MakeHuman, Mixamo + any Blender, Maya etc humanoid model as long as you import them into a Unity project and generate a "rig definition" file using our [url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/NightmarePuppeteerPublic/releases/tag/v1.0]free tool here[/url]

*Any fbx from any program is supported as a "prop"
*We made a[url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/NightmarePuppeteerPublic/releases/tag/v1.0] free script [/url]to convert virtually any humanoid 3d model that will work in Unity into an NP body or head
*We will make tutorials for this stuff and update the manual with it as soon as we finish adding the other new features

[/list]

Your character model does not need to be just a body or a head. You import complete models and NP will sever their heads or bodies for you. We do what we can.

To use your model again without having to re-import it, add it to NP's Steam Workshop by clicking the upload button after importing. A benefit of this is that others can use your models.

*NOTE - as far as I've seen Steam Workshop has TONS of copyrighted models in it so I don't think anyone cares as long as they are not sold. So upload Shrek or Batman or whatever the fuck you want ^_^

We'll be updating the import stuff regularly for the next week or two until the other new features are done before we go to work on our next animated feature film.

** This stuff is still in testing so expect bugs- please report them as comments to this post or here on [url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/NightmarePuppeteerPublic/issues]our github issues page[/url]. Thanks!

[b][DISCLAIMER] [/b][i]In order to use the clay stuff we had to upgrade the Unity project so this *might* have broken a lot of things. We hope not, but we created a new "testing" branch for this update as its probably unstable.

Also Unity(the game engine NP is made in) has removed the resolution/quality dialog that appeared when you launched the game so you are now unable to choose your resolution through the game. NP will use the default resolution of your display. NP is designed for 1920 x 1080 - 16.9 ratio. Choose this manually if things look weird. We'll build our own resolution selection menu later.

We added help text to the new clay menu's but HAVE NOT updated the manual yet. We will be adding a tutorial video shortly. Check out these introvideos for more info.[/i]

[previewyoutube=NP-o9n21JWA;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=cRlOnlkf-v0;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=20VJ1sjBusc;full][/previewyoutube]

To access the testing branch Right Click NP in your Steam Library and choose "Properties"  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38190375/a50854a9aae617d4ce61de2b9da2560f68555009.png[/img]

In the field "Enter Beta access..." enter letmebreakstuff and press the Check Code button- then in the popup choose the testing branch- you need to be on the "testing" branch.

Since there's a lot of new code the download is about 4.5gb- sorry about that- future updates will be smaller.

Please report any bugs you have to our [url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/NightmarePuppeteerPublic/issues]Github repo here[/url] or if thats too much trouble report them as comments to this post(screenshots etc are very helpful in fixing bugs)

Please submit any ideas you have for features/things you want to be able to do and we'll do our best.

By request we will be now be working on a Clay Prop Making menu where you'll be able to make props out of clay and use them in NP like any other prop(thanks Jolsh for the idea).

Then we will be adding body and head import to NP. You will be able to use any Daz, Mixamo, or Makehuman heads and bodies inside NP- we will also add better prop import.

If you want to see if your .fbx body will work in NP in the near future try adding it [url=https://ricardoreis.net/trilib/trilib2demo/avatarloader/]here[/url]

For props try [url=https://ricardoreis.net/trilib/trilib2demo/modelviewer/]here[/url]

That's the asset we are using(upgrading) so if your model works there it will work in NP in a future version.

That's all for now, please let us know how the clay works OR doesn't work haha.

So again, sorry there's no resolution/quality menu- Unity removed it and didn't provide a replacement so we'll make our own when this new stuff is in a non test/beta release.

notes.title: Nightmare Puppeteer can make you that sweet cryptocurrency
notes.content:
As a cryptocurrency enthusiast myself as I was designing Nightmare Puppeteer I added some things to it to help people create original art pieces with it.

If you've never heard of NFT digital art go read about it, its the next big thing for buying/selling art.

Here are just two of many NFT art markets
[url=https://www.superrare.co/]SuperRare[/url]
[url=https://opensea.io/]OpenSea[/url]

There are many more like those and many more on the way where artists are making good money for their art.

So what does this have to do with Nightmare Puppeteer? If you browse the art on those sites you will see that they are either still images or animated gif's. Nightmare Puppeteer can create both AND it can also export 360' images and 360' image sequences that you can turn into animated gif's etc.

Everything you make with NP is yours. So if I were you I'd use NP to create pieces of original art and sell them on those sites. Who knows? You can be the next big thing in digital art!

You need an Ethereum wallet to use those art sites. I recommend this one [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ur9YpD3X4Iw]Metamask[/url]. You'll also need a few dollars(usd) to process your art creation transactions. The last time I did it, it cost about $0.75 to create an NFT but the prices will vary. 

Now you might ask yourself why I, the creator of NP is not doing this. I'm just too busy.

I'm currently making a new animated feature film and I'm going to use Nightmare Puppeteer to create some footage of people talking on giant screens that appear in the film. Here is a test clip from the film [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ur9YpD3X4Iw]here[/url].

So my film "[url=https://github.com/mdotstrange/MDoll/wiki]M Doll[/url]" will be the first animated feature film that includes footage created in Nightmare Puppeteer.

On that note. If I were you I would create a full length film or pilot for a series in Nightmare Puppeteer and enter it into film festivals/try to sell it to Netflix etc.

All of this is totally possible and someone will do it in time. Why not you? If you all don't do it then I'm going to, but why should I have all the fun? GO DO IT!

notes.title: The Nightmare Puppeteer origin story....
notes.content:
Imagination Rabbits in house professional weirdo M dot Strange released an animated feature film titled "I am Nightmare" in 2014. You can see the trailer here
[previewyoutube=6K72Pq180_E;full][/previewyoutube]

The reason this film is relevant to Nightmare Puppeteer is because it was the first time M dot Strange utilized a basic automatic lip sync for the characters. This is done using a very simple technique where the audio amplitude of the voice drives the rotation of the jaw.

After completing the above film in 2014, M dot Strange went into video game development and finished several small games and experiments you can [url=https://mdotstrange.itch.io/]find here on his itch.io page.[/url]

In 2017 he decided to recreate his simple lip sync system inside of the Unity game engine just to make some fast animations. This animation was made using that technique
[previewyoutube=mt3f1KIr5PI;full][/previewyoutube]

After making that animation using the lip sync technique M dot decided to push the technique further and turn it into a weird little game/toy called "Weirdo" or "Weirdoware" It utilized the lip sync with a live microphone. The system analyzed the users voice and could detect pitch, causing different things to happen based on the pitch. You can see a video of it here
[previewyoutube=0gzoWmkGvcI;full][/previewyoutube]

You can download and play with [url=https://mdotstrange.itch.io/weird]Weirdoware for free here[/url]

In early 2020 M dot dug out the Weirdro character with its lip sync system to make some more weird animations like this one
[previewyoutube=JAPUGtFr0v4;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]*If you look closely at Weirdro's head it is included in Nightmare Puppeteer with a different texture.[/i]

A few days after making the last video M dot pushed the concept further adding manual animation control and he created this animation with it
[previewyoutube=SMWPthKvub0;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]*The character in the above video is used in the short video that plays before every scene in Nightmare Puppeteer.[/i]

A day after that M dot pushed the concept further and made this animation in what was the first version of Nightmare Puppeteer
[previewyoutube=mGDwn0-2YO4;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]*The scene in the above video became the "Funny Haha" scene.[/i]

So now you know where Nightmare Puppeteer came from. May god have mercy on your soul.

Now go out and create and release your own original animations with Nightmare Puppeteer! 

You will write the next chapter in Nightmare Puppeteers history! Good luck Puppeteerians!
